features.feature_value: Uses strong insult/profanity and vulgar phrasing
features.rationale: The post contains highly taboo/inflammatory language targeting an outgroup.

features.feature_value: Explicit repeated profanity directed at political figures/groups
features.rationale: Direct use of the word “Fuck” twice with political targets is a strong lexical moderation cue.

features.feature_value: Dismissive, slangy framing of political actors
features.rationale: The post uses casual contempt terms (“garbage”) rather than policy discussion.

features.feature_value: Direct negative calls against specific political actors
features.rationale: The language is aimed at named political figure(s) and an international political target.

features.feature_value: Moral condemnation and contempt about actors enabling autocracy/serfdom
features.evidence_span: "fuck you I got mineing their base into autocracy."
features.rationale: Normative outrage/condemnation (“fuck you… autocracy”) indicates strongly negative evaluation tied to power abuse.

features.feature_value: Mirror re-targets blame from Trump/Vance camp to Biden/Kamala camp
features.evidence_span: "Trump is the worst" / "Biden was the worst"
features.rationale: The mirror swaps which party leader is blamed while keeping the same evaluative structure, signaling partisan antagonism.

features.feature_value: Direct rhetorical choice question to argue abortion stance
features.evidence_span: "Would you save a baby or 10 fertilized zygotes in a freezer?"
features.rationale: The conditional-choice framing is an argumentative structure commonly used in contentious policy debates.

features.feature_value: “Yes, … but we can’t …” juxtaposition of competing claims
features.evidence_span: "Yes, we have yearly school shootings, but we cant ban guns"
features.rationale: The text uses a contrastive ‘yes-but’ pattern to rebut a policy position.
